summary: Umar asks a man who greeted him how he is, then writes to Abu Moosa Ash'ari urging him to be content with the provision Allaah gives and to be grateful for it.
notes: Two separate reports: Anas (Umar and the greeting) and Hasan Basri (Umar's letter to Abu Moosa).

summary: Umar says the grateful always receive more from Allaah, so one should ask Allaah for more, citing Surah Ibraheem verse 7.
Uthmaan praises Allaah for not meeting a group of wrongdoers he was sent to deal with, and frees a slave as a sign of gratitude.

Ali says every bounty is followed by gratitude and gratitude brings increase, and that the doors of du'aa, acceptance, Taubah and forgiveness are never opened while others are closed, quoting the Qur'aan.
notes: Two separate sayings of Ali; the second begins 'Hadhrat Muhammad bin Ka'b Qurazi narrates'. The '(,)' is OCR debris. Matched to approved muhammad-bin-kab (unsure); the text adds 'Qurazi', so please confirm the match.

summary: Abu Dardaa calls a day without hardship a great bounty from Allaah, and says those who see Allaah's bounties only in food and drink have limited understanding.
notes: Two separate sayings of Abu Dardaa, the second introduced by 'Another narration quotes him'.

summary: Aa'isha says gratitude is due even for plain water drunk without difficulty, and Asmaa bint Abi Bakr falls into sajdah of gratitude after finding a keepsake from the Prophet that she had lost following Abdullaah bin Zubayr's martyrdom.
notes: Two separate reports: Aa'isha's saying and Asmaa's incident. The salaah tag is for the sajdah of gratitude, the nearest approved fit.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports that at Badr, when the Prophet's turn came to walk, Abu Lubaabah and a second companion offered to walk instead, and the Prophet refused, saying they were no less in need of reward than he was.
notes: OCR garbled the second companion's name ('Hadhrat and Hadhrat'), so he is left out rather than guessed (likely Ali, unverified). Garbled '(giif' and 'mi's' also ignored.

summary: Muttalib bin Abu Wadaa'ah reports that the Prophet said the salaah of one who prays seated is half the reward of standing, and the Sahabah then strove to pray standing.
notes: Muttalib bin Abu Wadaa'ah is not the approved entry muttalib-bin-saaib-bin-abu-wadaaah (a different name), so kept as null.

summary: When the Muslims in Madinah were ill with fever and could pray only seated, the Prophet said seated prayer is half the reward, and the Sahabah then struggled to stand in prayer despite their weakness.
notes: Two chains (Anas; Abdullaah bin Amr) for the same event, kept as one narration.

summary: Rabaa'ah bin Ka'b, who served the Prophet, asks for companionship in Jannah, and the Prophet tells him to help himself by making much sajdah.
notes: Not the approved rabeeah-bin-ibaad, so a new entry. The second version ('Hadhrat Rabee'ah (RA)') is the same person's variant and is not tagged separately.

summary: Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith describes coming to the Prophet with a delegation, accepting Islaam and pledging allegiance, and refusing a worldly grant because he prefers to ask the Prophet for help in the Aakhirah.

people.name: Abdul Jabbaar bin Haarith bin Maalik Hadasi Manaari

notes: OCR badly garbled the greeting and the Islaam formula, so those are not represented. Tameem Daari is his cousin who asked for the grant.

summary: Amr bin Taghlib reports the Prophet praising him for trusting the independence Allaah placed in his heart when others were given gifts, and Amr says he would not trade those words for red camels.
notes: Stray OCR '(!2)' ignored.

summary: Ali and Umar see a Bedouin carrying his mother around the Tawaaf, and Ali urges Umar to go round again so that the mercy coming down on the Bedouin may reach them too, both reciting couplets.
notes: OCR garbled the attribution ('Addressing Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat All said'); roles follow the text. The Bedouin is unnamed and left out.

summary: Abdullaah bin Umar frees a shepherd who had escaped with him from the captors of his camel, declines to reclaim the camel so as to keep the reward, and is urged by his sister Hafsah to marry so that his children either earn reward for patience or pray for him.
notes: Three separate narrations: Maymoon bin Mahraan (camel and shepherd), a later report of the camel being sold, and Amr bin Dinaar (marriage). Najdah's sahabi status is unsure. The shepherd and the people from Haroora are unnamed and left out.

summary: Ammaar bin Yaasir, on the way to Siffeen, prays that he would gladly risk death for Allaah's pleasure and trusts that Allaah will never let him fail while he acts to please Him.
notes: Abdur Rahmaan bin Abza is not in the approved list; sahabi yes from the RA in the text.

summary: Abdullaah bin Amr says a good deed done now is dearer to him than two liked deeds done in the Prophet's time, because the world has now come to the Sahabah while they were then focused on the Aakhirah.
notes: The Prophet is mentioned only as the time of companionship.

summary: Alqama asks Aa'isha whether the Prophet set aside particular days for worship, and she replies that his deeds were constant, and that no one can do what he did.
notes: The text speaks of worship in general, so salaah is the nearest approved worship theme. Please review.

summary: Mughiera bin Shu'ba reports that the Prophet stood in salaah until his feet split, and when asked why, given that Allaah had forgiven his past and future errors, he said he should be a grateful servant.
notes: The closing line is a cross-reference to the chapter on salaah; the questioner is unnamed.

summary: Zubayr bin Abdullaah reports, through his grandmother Zuhaymah, that Uthmaan fasted continually and prayed through the night, sleeping only briefly at the start.
notes: The heading and text give 'Utnmaan' (OCR for Uthmaan). Zubayr bin Abdullaah is not the approved zubayr (Ibn Awwaam); his sahabi status is assumed no, so please confirm.

summary: Mujaahid says Abdullaah bin Zubayr's worship was unmatched, and that during a flood, when people could not perform Tawaaf, he went round the Ka'bah several times by swimming.
notes: No approved worship theme fits Tawaaf; salaah is used as the nearest fit. A 'tawaaf' or general 'worship' id may be better. Please review.

summary: Two chains report that Abdullaah bin Zubayr fasted seven days in a row until his insides dried, and that when very old he reduced it to three days.
notes: Two chains for the same fact, kept as one narration. The closing line is a cross-reference to later chapters.

summary: Anas describes the Prophet as the most handsome, generous and bravest of people, who rode Abu Talha's horse to investigate a night alarm in Madinah and reassured the people, and says the Sahabah sought refuge with him whenever battle grew fierce.
notes: Three parts: Anas's account of the alarm, a second narration (the horse named Mandoob), and a separate statement that they took refuge with the Prophet in battle. The Prophet's horse-as-ocean remark is tagged miracles-and-blessings.

summary: An unnamed Companion says that at Badr they sheltered by the side of the Prophet, because he was the fiercest of fighters.
notes: The speaker's name is lost in OCR ('Hadhrat (RA)'). The heading mentions Anas and Ali, but the text does not name the speaker, so no person is tagged.

summary: Baraa bin Aazib says the Prophet did not desert at Hunayn, describing the Hawaazin archers and the Prophet remaining on his white mule, with Abu Sufyaan holding its reins, while declaring he is a Nabi without a lie.
notes: The text says only 'Abu Sufyaan'. Tagged as Abu Sufyaan bin Haarith bin Abdil Muttalib, who the standard hadith names as holding the mule's reins at Hunayn. The approved abu-sufyaan is Abu Sufyaan bin Harb. Please confirm. The man from Qais is unnamed and left out. OCR garbled the quotation marks.

summary: Baraa continues that the Prophet dismounted and prayed for help, and that in the battle only the bravest could fight beside him.
notes: Continues the Hunayn account begun in the previous narration. The closing cross-reference lists earlier Companions from the chapter on jihaad; they are not part of this narration and are left out.

summary: Abdullaah bin Amr reports that the Prophet ate a date he found by his side, then stayed awake fearing it might have been one of the Sadaqah dates.
notes: The text ends mid-sentence ('one of those,') and the narration appears to be cut off. The wife who asks is unnamed.

summary: Ibn Seereen says Abu Bakr alone forced himself to vomit food he had eaten, and Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla recounts that the food came from Ibn Nu'aymaan's paid incantation, which Abu Bakr then vomited out on learning its source.
notes: Two separate reports: Ibn Seereen and Abdur Rahmaan bin Abu Layla. The text opens with heading debris ('Abu Bakr ■'). Ibn Nu'aymaan is not in the approved list, and his full name is not given in the text. The people asking for a cure are unnamed.

summary: Zaid bin Arqam reports that Abu Bakr's slave brought food from incantations he had performed for pay, and that Abu Bakr ate a morsel, then forced himself to vomit it out, fearing the Prophet's warning about a body fed by unlawful food.
notes: The slave is unnamed and left out. The Prophet is mentioned only through Abu Bakr's quotation.

summary: Zaid bin Aslam reports that Umar, finding the taste of some milk strange, learnt it came from zakaah camels and vomited it out.
notes: The heading is garbled ('llnrar'), so Umar is taken from the text. The herders and the water-bag carrier are unnamed.

summary: Miswar bin Makhrama recounts sticking close to Umar, and Sha'bi reports that Ali, learning that a householder was a money-changer, refused to drink from his well and to take shade under a tax collector's property, citing the Prophet.
notes: Two parts: Miswar's fragment, which is cut off after 'stuck close to Hadhrat Umar', and Sha'bi's report about Ali in Kufa. Sha'bi is not in the approved list. The little girl and householder are unnamed.

summary: Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that Mu'aadh bin Jabal, who had two wives, treated them equally, and that when both died in the Shaam plague he drew lots to decide which would be placed first in their shared grave.
notes: The second version (Mu'aadh not drinking from the house of the wife whose turn it was not) is a variant on the same trait, kept as one narration.

summary: Tawoos reports that Abdullaah bin Abbaas, asked when Umar left Arafaat, declined to say out of caution, which surprised the people.
notes: OCR garbled 'Umar !s9SiK' in the report of Umar reciting the Talbiya. The 'Tawakkul' heading is appended to the text. The man asking is unnamed.

summary: Not a narration: the text is only the phrase 'Rasulullaah ﷺ' under a section heading.
notes: Heading fragment only. Nothing to tag; the Prophet is only named.

summary: Jaabir narrates that a Bedouin drew the Prophet's sword while he slept under a tree, and when the Prophet woke and asked who would save him, the Bedouin said Allaah, and the Prophet did not punish him.
notes: Jaabir is a participant who tells part of his own story, so subject. The Bedouin is unnamed and left out.

summary: Jaabir narrates that at Nakhlah, Ghowrath bin Haarith stood over the sleeping Prophet with a sword, the sword fell from his hand, and the Prophet let him go after he pledged not to fight him or join those who did.
notes: The text ends by saying the narration continues to explain Salaatul Khowf. Ghowrath's sahabi status is unsure, since he was not yet a Muslim at this point.

summary: Yahya bin Murrah narrates that Ali, when guarded at night, said that guarding does not help against what is decreed, that angels protect a person until his decreed time, and that no one tastes the sweetness of Imaan unless convinced of qadr.
notes: The name is garbled in OCR ('Hadhrat Mi (RA)'); Ali is taken from the heading. The guards are unnamed.

summary: Qataadah reports that Ali was restless on his last night, that his family urged him not to go out, and that he said angels protect a person until destiny comes, then went to the Masjid and was assassinated.
notes: The text says Qataadah (RA). Matched to approved qataada (no), since a Companion could not report Ali's last night with certainty. Please confirm. The family is unnamed.

summary: Abu Mijlaz reports that when a man warned Ali of a plot, Ali said a person's appointed term is his guard, and Yahya bin Katheer adds that Ali said the same when people offered to guard him.
notes: The man from the Muraad tribe is unnamed. Footnote debris '(fl)' ignored.

summary: A narrator (name garbled in the OCR) reports that when Ali judged a dispute while sitting at the base of a wall, one man said the wall was about to fall, and Ali told him to continue because Allaah suffices, and the wall fell after Ali had left.
notes: The narrator's name is garbled in OCR ('Hadhrat Muhammad ﷺ'); it is omitted rather than guessed, to avoid confusion with the Prophet. The two disputants are unnamed.

summary: Abu Dhabiyya reports that Uthmaan visited Abdullaah bin Mas'ood on his deathbed and offered a stipend for his daughters, and that Abdullaah declined, telling them to recite Surah Waaqi'ah nightly because the Prophet said poverty would never afflict its reciter.
notes: Abu Dhabiyya matched to approved abu-dhabyaan (unsure) on spelling; please confirm. The closing sentence is a cross-reference to Abu Bakr and Abu Dardaa, who are not tagged. The daughters are unnamed.
